in_arabic.name: ياسمينة
in_arabic.meaning: اسم يدل على الورد الجميل والرائع
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم ياسمينة مشتق من الاسم العربي ياسمين، وهو نوع من أنواع الورد ذي الرائحة الجميلة والمنظر الرائع. ورد في القرآن الكريم ذكر الورد والياسمين في سياق الجنة والخيرات. يعتبر اسم ياسمينة من الأسماء التي تحمل معاني الورود والزهور، مما يعكس الجمال والروعة.

data.cultural_impact: The name Yasmeenah carries a deep cultural significance rooted in Arabic and Islamic literature and history. Jasmine is one of the most beloved flowers in the Arab world, highly valued for its exquisite fragrance. It is claimed that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) himself praised the beauty of jasmine and compared it to the Garden of Paradise. In several Arabic and Islamic stories, Yasmeenah is the name of a beautiful and virtuous heroine or the beloved of a valiant hero. Furthermore, this floral name is often used as a symbol of grace, beauty, and strength in the Arab and Islamic culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Yasmeenah represents the exalted qualities of purity, tranquility, and divine intoxication. According to Sufi interpretation, the heart full of the love for God is compared to a blooming jasmine flower, releasing its fragrance of closeness to the Divine. Additionally, Yasmeenah is one of the names given to the beloved%20http://islamicfeminine.arts.sbc.edu/encyclopedia/aye_5689.html Ayya Kitam in the famous "Conference of the Birds" by Rumi, referring to the spiritual journey of the seeker towards union with the Beloved. Thus, carrying the name Yasmeenah bestows both a spiritual and cultural connection to the cherished traditions, values, and ideals of the Arab and Islamic world.
